resources.string: Read this carefully. Whospair works differently from the messaging apps you know, and some of those differences cannot be undone.
Whospair has no server. Messages and calls travel directly between devices. Nobody — including us — sits in the middle, stores your data, or can hand it over.

No operator stands behind this app. What you send, to whom, and what you do with what you receive is entirely your responsibility. Whospair is a tool: its authors cannot be held liable for how you use it or its consequences.
No authority reviews, filters, or removes content. There is no report button that reaches anyone, because there is no one to reach.
Messages are end-to-end encrypted (X25519 and AES-256-GCM) and signed. Calls go over Tor, encrypted with a key that changes about every ten seconds.
Your identity, contacts, and messages exist only on this device. Uninstalling the app erases them.
Your identity is a cryptographic key, not an account. If you lose it, it is gone. There is no password reset, no support line, no backup we can restore.
Privacy tools protect legitimate conversations. Using Whospair to break the law remains breaking the law.
This software is provided as is, without guarantee of availability, correctness, or fitness for any particular purpose.
Encryption protects data in transit. It cannot protect a device that is already compromised by malware, a rootkit, or someone holding it.
Continuing means you understand the above, and specifically that a lost identity cannot be recovered.
I have read and accept these terms
Whospair cannot run without accepting them. The app will close.
Messaging and calls that leave no trace on any server, because there is no server.
There are no usernames or phone numbers. You exchange keys directly.
Scan their code, or let them scan yours
A new identity means a new code. Sharing it again is the only way back.
Every message carries an expiry from the moment you send it.
Type, then pick how long it should live
Pick the lifetime that fits what you are saying. When it runs out, the message is deleted on both devices.
Shorter is safer. Anything still on screen is still on disk.

The screen opens only for you

The screen opens only when you are the one looking at it. For anyone else, or if no one is looking, it stays black.

If your face changes (injury, swelling, beard, glasses), it may no longer be recognized and the screen will stay black. At the bottom of the screen, "Turn off hiding with the PIN" always works with your unlock code. You can then record your face again.

This button follows the same rules as the lock screen: your duress PIN, typed here, erases everything, and so do 10 wrong codes.

It protects against prying eyes; it is not a lock: your PIN remains the real protection. Everything happens on the phone: your face is kept as encrypted numbers, never as a photo.
